source.title: A General Framework to Enhance Fine-tuning-based LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Jie Ren; Zhenwei Dai; Xianfeng Tang; Hui Liu; Jingying Zeng; Zhen Li; Rahul Goutam; Suhang Wang; Yue Xing; Qi He; Hui Liu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests the proposed recovery mechanism and two recovery attacks using its own experiments, but on GRUN and with measurements different from the original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper's own PCA, separability, and mixed-question experiments bear on whether gradient-based unlearning distinguishes and suppresses target data. Its paraphrasing and quantization experiments report GRUN's unlearning effectiveness under those attacks. Cited attack or unlearning findings from other papers are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: Section 3 uses representation analysis to argue that GA-based unlearning (GD, NPO) on TOFU suppresses target data rather than erasing it (version C, analysis branch). Section 5.3 attacks the authors' new method GRUN with GPT-4 paraphrasing and quantization, which bears on F and, for that method only, on D and E. Tables 2 and 3 also report vanilla GD/NPO/IDK/RMU unlearning and utility, which bears on the accuracy and utility part of A.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that GA-based unlearning does not erase target data but recognizes it and suppresses related outputs, like suppression-based methods. On that basis they propose GRUN (soft gate plus ReFT), reporting better unlearning and utility, efficiency, sequential-unlearning gains, and stable effectiveness under paraphrasing and quantization. The robustness claim is a Section 5.3 result, not part of the stated conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: GRUN uses a gated representation fine-tuning module rather than the unlearning recipes in the original sources; the robustness tests are performed on GRUN.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack type (prompt paraphrasing versus model quantization), model, and unlearning loss (GD, NPO, IDK) vary in Table 5. The paper also reports that using adjacent rather than interval layers changes unlearning performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Across four model×method cells, more separated target/retain embeddings (lower CSD) go with lower forget-set ROUGE-L (Table 1). The text misnames which cell is lowest.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The degree of representational separation of forget data predicts how strongly GA-based unlearning suppresses its recall.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The attack table does not provide numeric un-attacked baselines or uncertainty estimates. The attack evidence covers only GRUN, GPT-4 paraphrasing, and quantization; it does not test recovery via fine-tuning or activation ablation.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying reported results were left out.

untested.parts: No simple attack is applied to the vanilla methods (GD, NPO, IDK, RMU). Only the accuracy and utility part is reported.
Relearning or fine-tuning attacks are not tested at all.

No activation-direction ablation is performed, and no hidden knowledge is actually recovered from GA-unlearned models. The evidence is embedding geometry and mixed-prompt suppression only, on TOFU. RMU and IDK are not analysed.
Quantization is never applied to vanilla unlearned models. Bit width is unstated. WMDP is not tested under attack.
Only GPT-4 paraphrasing is tested, and only on GRUN. Jailbreaks, other languages and in-context information are not tested.
GRUN is not tested against relearning, activation ablation, jailbreaks or WMDP attacks.

missing.what: PCA of target/retain/never-seen embeddings before vs after GD/NPO unlearning, showing target data moved to a distinct region. This is the core evidence for C.
Vanilla and GRUN forget-set ROUGE-L/Probability and utility on TOFU (5%/10%), needed as un-attacked baselines for Table 5 and for A's utility cost.
WMDP bio/cyber accuracy and MMLU for before, vanilla RMU and GRUN-RMU on both models.
Normal-Q&A ROUGE-L values with and without mixed target data.

record.verdict_notes: Reader version codes V3–V6 map to C–F. The attacks test only the authors' own method, with no vanilla positive control, so the D/E/F evidence is weak. Quantization bit width is unspecified, and the ptgt used in Table 5 is unspecified. The text's description of Table 1 contradicts the table on which cell has the lowest CSD. This is not an original source for any version.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports unlearning and utility results, but does not test whether the original unlearning methods in this version resist the specified simple attacks.
No attack using a small unrelated, loosely related, or subset relearning set is evaluated.
No activation-direction ablation is performed; the paper tests the alternative mechanism claim through representation analysis and mixed prompts.
Quantization is tested on GRUN; the paper does not state the bit width in the presented results or test other unlearning methods under quantization.
Prompt paraphrasing is tested on GRUN. Jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information are not tested.
The paper tests GRUN against paraphrasing and quantization, not against fine-tuning or activation ablation.

relation.reason: The study reports its own attacks and a representation analysis that bear on versions C, D, E and F.

tranche.reason: GRUN is a different method aimed at the same question. Its paraphrase and quantization tests bear on D/E/F, and the Section 3 representation analysis of GD/NPO bears on C.

source_check.notes: Table 5 columns are inferred as paraphrase Llama/Mistral, then quantization Llama/Mistral. Table 5 does not state the target split (5%/10%), dataset or metric; presumably TOFU forget ROUGE-L. Only GRUN was attacked and the bit width is unstated. Rows r13-r24 carry state 'absent' (no recovery), which for F means robustness is observed. Vanilla RMU on Mistral loses 0.052 MMLU, a moderate utility cost behind l5.

statements.correction: Llama 3.1 8B and Mistral v0.1 7B, GD and NPO, TOFU. Fig 1 PCA: target, retain and never-seen embeddings are similar before unlearning. After unlearning, target embeddings sit in a distinct region far from the others. Table 1: lower CSD goes with lower forget ROUGE-L (Mistral GD: CSD 0.13, ROUGE-L 0.001; Llama NPO: 3.21, 0.197). Fig 2: adding target questions lowers ROUGE-L on normal questions (no numbers in the text). No knowledge recovery was tested.
statements.problem: Nothing is said about this study except the r9 citation. r9 is a drop in normal-Q&A ROUGE-L on mixed prompts, not a similarity measure. Fig 1 shows the reverse of 'stay close to the original': after unlearning, target embeddings move far from retain and never-seen data. The study supports C through recognition plus suppression, not through representation similarity.

statements.correction: GRUN on Llama 3.1 8B and Mistral v0.1 7B, quantization of unstated bit width: forget ROUGE-L 0.005/0.000 (GD), 0.000/0.000 (NPO), 0.040/0.034 (IDK), Llama/Mistral (Table 5). Only GRUN was quantized.
Only GRUN-unlearned models were attacked, by quantization and by paraphrasing. Vanilla GD, NPO and IDK models were not attacked.

GRUN (GD/NPO/IDK losses), Llama 3.1 8B and Mistral v0.1 7B, TOFU setup. Quantized forget ROUGE-L is 0.000-0.040 (Table 5), against un-attacked GRUN 0.000-0.040 (Table 2). Bit width and scheme are not stated. The authors' own test; no vanilla model was quantized as a control.
statements.problem: Cites r19-r24 but says nothing about GRUN. The stated conditions (4-bit/8-bit, WMDP and MUSE, Llama/Qwen/Zephyr/ICLM) do not cover this study, which uses TOFU, includes Mistral v0.1 and gives no bit width. There is no un-quantized pairing in Table 5.
